A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Distilled Decoding work. All 25 pages of each version, including Appendices A–F, are available and readable; their text, equations, tables, figures, and generated images support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VAR and LlamaGen distillation experiments on ImageNet-256 and LAION-COCO, including quantitative results in Tables 1–3 and ablations in Figures 7–8.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments, quantitative results, ablations, and generated-image examples in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The flow-matching construction, distillation objective, and sampling procedures in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–4 are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same prediction heads, embeddings, and attention modifications.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-256 for class-conditional generation and LAION-COCO for text-to-image generation. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical comparator membership, including pretrained VAR and LlamaGen, skip-n and onestep* baselines, and the other generative models listed in Table 1.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same model sizes, training budgets, sampling settings, and evaluation procedures. The 1.2M class-conditional training pairs, 3M text-to-image training pairs, and 5k evaluation prompts are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 and Appendix D retain the same training-duration, intermediate-timestep, and dataset-size analyses in Figures 7–8. Appendix F contains the same qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The tables and training curves retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains one-step FIDs of 9.94 for VAR-d16-DD and 11.35 for LlamaGen-L-DD; Table 3 retains the two-step text-to-image FID of 28.95.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, Proposition 3.1, and Appendix A proof are unchanged. Changing two references or headings from 'Prop. 3.1' to 'Thm. 3.1' is a labeling edit, not a mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty, one-step generation, training-data independence, and speed–quality claims. Their numerical supporting claims are also unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of generation quality, scaling, and sensitivity remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the teacher-dependent quality limitation and challenges of applying DD to LLMs; Appendix E retains the same discussion of possible extensions.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain identical architecture details, solver configuration, optimizer settings, loss weights, and EMA settings. Code and pretrained-model release statements and resource links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 4 and Appendix E are unchanged, including comparisons with DMD and MAR. The publication-status header does not alter the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 replaces 'Preprint' with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' and changes appendix references from 'App.' to 'Sec.' Two 'Prop. 3.1' labels become 'Thm. 3.1', although the statement still says 'Proposition 3.1'. The narrative and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Presentation edits are limited to the publication header, arXiv version/date stamp, and appendix-reference wording in the captions of Figures 1–2. Figure artwork, plots, table structures, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations throughout the main text and appendices. Publication-header and reference-label edits do not materially improve the paper. The introduced proposition/theorem labeling inconsistency is a small editorial blemish without a meaningful overall quality effect.
